question.text: Chapter 9 lists FIVE categories of 'Special Situation Assets' that an SSF can invest in. Which of the following is NOT on the Chapter 9 list?

answer.text: Stressed Loans available for acquisition under Clause 58 of RBI Master Direction — Transfer of Loan Exposure Directions, 2021.
Security Receipts issued by an ARC registered with the RBI.
Securities of investee companies whose loans have been downgraded to 'D' or equivalent after 90+ days default.
Listed futures and options of Nifty index constituents.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 9 lists: (a) stressed loans under RBI Clause 58; (b) SRs from RBI-registered ARCs; (c) securities of investee companies whose stressed loans are available for acquisition; (d) securities where SRs have been issued against the borrowings; (e) securities where disclosed default > 90 days and credit rating downgraded to D. Nifty F&O is listed-derivatives — Cat III territory, not SSF. The Trap: Options A, B, C are verbatim from the Chapter 9 SSF list. Option D is a Cat III strategy and is excluded from SSF scope. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-B / XIX-E (Cat III) cover listed F&O. XIX-A covers SSF asset list at sales level. III-A/C (Compliance) covers 90-day NPA norm under RBI. Manager's Pro-Tip: Build an SSF investment universe tracker that auto-flags asset eligibility daily (rating changes, IBC admissions, 90-day default marks). Internal audit should reconcile this against the SEBI SSF-specific asset list every quarter.
